title: Data Engineering with Spark & Kafka
subtitle: Batch and streaming pipelines with Apache Spark, Apache Kafka and lakehouse tables
audience_line: Data analysts, developers and engineers moving into data engineering
overview: This programme teaches participants to build batch and streaming data pipelines with open-source tools and Confluent Schema Registry. They see how big data processing moved from HDFS and MapReduce to object storage and the lakehouse, process data with Spark DataFrames and Spark SQL, store it in Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg tables, and tune Spark jobs. They then run Kafka on KRaft, process event streams with Spark Structured Streaming, integrate systems with Kafka Connect and Schema Registry, and schedule and check pipelines with Airflow and data quality tests. Every chapter ends with a lab on a local stack, and the programme closes with a final project: real-time order analytics built and presented by each team.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Data analysts, developers and engineers moving into data engineering

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Python, pandas and SQL (course: Python for Data Science), or equivalent. These are used, not taught

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 33 h: 27 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs on one dataset carried through every phase

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant (16 GB RAM minimum, Docker, VS Code, Jupyter) with a Docker Compose stack prepared by the trainer: Spark, Kafka 4 (KRaft), Schema Registry, Kafka Connect, Airflow 3, MinIO and an Iceberg REST catalog, services started per phase; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can build, tune and schedule batch and streaming pipelines with Spark and Kafka that write reliable lakehouse tables and pass data quality checks

phases.name: Spark Foundations
phases.focus: From Hadoop to the lakehouse, Spark architecture, DataFrames and Spark SQL
phases.intro: Participants see why data platforms moved from HDFS and MapReduce to object storage and the lakehouse, learn how Spark plans and runs work across a cluster, then transform data with DataFrames, Spark SQL and user-defined functions. Validated lab: a Spark job that cleans and aggregates the course dataset from object storage.

chapters.title: Big Data Foundations
chapters.content: From HDFS and MapReduce to object storage and the lakehouse

chapters.title: Spark Architecture
chapters.content: Driver, executors, jobs, stages, lazy evaluation

chapters.title: DataFrames & Spark SQL
chapters.content: DataFrame API, Spark SQL, user-defined functions

phases.name: Lakehouse Tables & Performance
phases.focus: Parquet, Delta Lake and Iceberg, partitioning, joins, adaptive query execution
phases.intro: Participants store results in open table formats that bring transactions, time travel and schema evolution to object storage, then make Spark jobs faster with partitioning, caching, the right joins and adaptive query execution, reading the Spark UI to find the bottleneck. Validated lab: a Delta or Iceberg table updated with a merge and read at an earlier version, and a slow job made measurably faster.

chapters.title: Table Formats
chapters.content: Parquet, Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg: ACID tables, time travel, schema evolution

chapters.title: Spark Performance
chapters.content: Partitioning, caching, joins, adaptive query execution, Spark UI

phases.name: Streaming, Integration & Orchestration
phases.focus: Kafka on KRaft, Structured Streaming, Kafka Connect, Schema Registry, Airflow
phases.intro: Participants run Kafka on KRaft and learn topics, partitions, producers and consumer groups, process event streams with Spark Structured Streaming using windows and watermarks, connect external systems with Kafka Connect and enforce schemas with Schema Registry, then schedule pipelines with Airflow and add data quality checks. Validated lab: a stream of events aggregated per minute into a lakehouse table, with late events handled by a watermark.

chapters.title: Kafka Fundamentals
chapters.content: KRaft clusters, topics, partitions, producers, consumer groups, delivery semantics

chapters.title: Structured Streaming with Kafka
chapters.content: Streaming queries, windows, watermarks, sinks, exactly-once output

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: Real-time order analytics, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three build a real-time analytics pipeline for an online shop's orders, reusing the phase labs, then present it as they would to a data team lead.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, produce order events to Kafka with a registered schema, aggregate them with Structured Streaming into Delta or Iceberg tables

chapters.title: Schedule, Check & Document
chapters.content: A daily batch job scheduled by Airflow, data quality checks, a Jupyter notebook dashboard and a short design note

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo with a burst of orders; questions and feedback

project.title: Real-Time Order Analytics
project.brief: Order events produced to Kafka with a registered schema, aggregated by Spark Structured Streaming into Delta or Iceberg tables, completed by a daily batch job scheduled in Airflow, checked by data quality tests and shown on a dashboard.
project.stack: Apache Kafka (KRaft), Schema Registry, Apache Spark (Structured Streaming, Spark SQL), Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg, MinIO, Apache Airflow, Python, Jupyter
project.deliverable: Pipeline code, design note, dashboard, live demo
